claims.text: The FY2025 10-K (period ended September 30, 2025) states: "We offer multiple affiliation options, which we refer to as AdvisorChoice®. Financial advisors primarily affiliate with us directly as either employees or independent contractors or as employees of third-party Registered Investment Advisors (“RIAs”) and broker-dealers to which we provide services through our RIA and Custody Services (“RCS”) division."

Raymond James's affiliation-options recruiting page (page content as of April 21, 2026) describes AdvisorChoice® as a platform of dynamic options and the freedom to choose among them, letting advisors match their professional goals to the affiliation option that is right for them.

The affiliation options listed on Raymond James's recruiting page (page content as of April 21, 2026) include: "Traditional Employee: Get everything you expect from working for a firm with a powerful difference – book ownership. Advisor Select: Lead your own branch with access to administrative support and full corporate benefits. Independent Contractor: Operate as an independent financial advisor backed by the resources of a national leader. Bank & Credit Union: Leverage national strength and local impact to grow your advisory business. Corporate RIA: Exercise true autonomy and support refined for fee-only practices under our established RIA."

The FY2025 10-K (period ended September 30, 2025) states: "Employee financial advisors work in a traditional branch supported by local management and administrative staff. They provide services predominantly to retail clients. Compensation for these financial advisors primarily includes a payout on revenues they generate and such advisors also participate in the firm’s employee benefit plans."

Under the Traditional Employee model, per Raymond James's affiliation-options page (page content as of April 21, 2026), advisors receive up to a 50% payout plus a full array of competitive employee benefits offerings, with a minimum of 5 years of experience required.

Under the Advisor Select model, per Raymond James's affiliation-options page (page content as of April 21, 2026), advisors receive a 70-80% gross payout plus a full array of competitive employee benefits offerings, and run their own branch (an employee affiliation option for advisors who want to lead a team).

Under the Independent Contractor model, per Raymond James's affiliation-options page (page content as of April 21, 2026), advisors receive an 81% to 90% payout and leverage Raymond James' third-party partnerships to build their own benefits package.

The FY2025 10-K (period ended September 30, 2025) states: "Our financial advisors who are independent contractors are generally responsible for all of their direct costs and, accordingly, receive a higher payout percentage on the revenues they generate than employee financial advisors."

On the fiscal 2Q26 earnings call (period ended March 31, 2026), management said independent payouts are higher than employee payouts because independent advisors cover their own overhead costs, real estate, and health insurance, while even on the employee side Raymond James has tiered payout systems, so as production increases an advisor moves higher up on the payout grid.

The FY2025 10-K (period ended September 30, 2025) states: "Independent contractor financial advisors may affiliate with us directly or through an affiliated bank or credit union in our Financial Institutions Division. With specific approval, and on a limited basis, they are permitted to conduct certain other approved business activities, such as offering insurance products, independent registered investment advisory services, and accounting and tax services."

On the fiscal 3Q26 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2026), management said Raymond James is agnostic about how an advisor affiliates (employee vs independent contractor vs RIA custody), wanting advisors to choose based on fit with its culture, values, platform and capabilities.

Raymond James's 2025 Investor Day deck (published June 5, 2025) presents the affiliation spectrum ranging from employee (RJA) to independent contractor (ICD) to RIA & Custody Services, including Employee Advisor (RJA), Advisor Select, Independent Advisor (ICD), Banks and Credit Unions, IAR (Corporate RIA), and RIA & Custody Services, described by Raymond James as servicing the largest addressable market in the industry.

The FY2025 10-K (period ended September 30, 2025) states that employee financial advisors work in a traditional branch and their compensation primarily includes a payout on revenues they generate, plus participation in the firm's employee benefit plans.

Under the Traditional Employee model, per Raymond James's affiliation-options page (page content as of April 21, 2026), advisors receive up to a 50% payout plus the full array of competitive employee benefits offerings.

Under the Advisor Select model, per Raymond James's affiliation-options page (page content as of April 21, 2026), advisors receive a 70-80% gross payout plus the full array of competitive employee benefits offerings.

Under the Independent Contractor model, per Raymond James's affiliation-options page (page content as of April 21, 2026), advisors receive an 81% to 90% payout and build their own benefits package through third-party partnerships.

Under the Bank & Credit Union model, per Raymond James's affiliation-options page (page content as of April 21, 2026), advisors receive a competitive compensation package from the financial institution in partnership with Raymond James.

Under the Corporate RIA model, per Raymond James's affiliation-options page (page content as of April 21, 2026), advisors receive an 81% to 90% payout and build their own benefits package through third-party partnerships.

Under the RIA & Custody Services model, per Raymond James's affiliation-options page (page content as of April 21, 2026), advisors work with their RIA or broker/dealer to determine compensation and create their own benefits package.

On the fiscal 2Q26 earnings call (period ended March 31, 2026), management said independent advisor payouts are higher than employee payouts because independent advisors cover their own overhead costs, real estate, and health insurance.

On the fiscal 2Q26 earnings call (period ended March 31, 2026), management said even on the employee side Raymond James has tiered payout systems, so as production increases advisors get higher up on the payout grid.

On the fiscal 4Q24 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2024), management said that for RIA custody the margin on a P&L basis is actually higher because the attachment revenue booked is much lower, whereas in Raymond James's other businesses it grosses up the revenues pre-payout, and ROCA varies with the RIA's asset mix and pricing structure.

The FY2025 10-K (period ended September 30, 2025) states that for firms affiliated through the RIA and Custody Services division, revenues related to their assets in the PCG segment are included in Account and service fees.
As of September 30, 2025, Raymond James reported 8,943 total financial advisors, consisting of 3,878 employee financial advisors and 5,065 independent contractor advisors.
As of September 30, 2024, Raymond James reported 8,787 total financial advisors, consisting of 3,826 employees and 4,961 independent contractors.
As of September 30, 2023, Raymond James reported 8,712 total financial advisors, consisting of 3,693 employees and 5,019 independent contractors.

On the fiscal 4Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), management said Raymond James ended fiscal 2025 with a record number of financial advisors, 2% higher than the prior year, reflecting solid advisor retention and strong recruiting results.

On the fiscal 4Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), management reported record trailing 12-month production for recruited financial advisors of $407 million for fiscal 2025, in the domestic independent contractor and employee channels.

On the fiscal 3Q26 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2026), management said through the first 9 months of fiscal 2026 Raymond James recruited advisors with trailing 12-month production totaling $393 million.

On the fiscal 3Q26 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2026), management said recruited advisors represented more than $56 billion of client assets at their previous firms through the first 9 months of fiscal 2026.

In the fiscal third quarter (ended June 30, 2026), Raymond James recruited financial advisors to its domestic independent contractor and employee channels with trailing 12-month production totaling $156 million and nearly $23 billion of client assets at their previous firms.

In the fiscal second quarter (ended March 31, 2026), Raymond James recruited financial advisors to its domestic independent contractor and employee channels with trailing 12-month production totaling $141 million and nearly $21 billion of client assets at their previous firms, the second-highest quarterly result in its history.
The FY2025 10-K (period ended September 30, 2025) states that for the year ended September 30, 2025, Raymond James's domestic financial advisor retention remained very strong.

On the fiscal 3Q26 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2026), CEO Paul Shoukry said Raymond James reports a 97% advisor satisfaction rate with its surveys, the best he knows of in the industry, and cited this retention as the foundation for growth.

Raymond James defines domestic Private Client Group net new assets as domestic Private Client Group client inflows, including dividends and interest, less domestic Private Client Group client outflows, including commissions, advisory fees, and other fees.

On the fiscal 3Q26 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2026), management said Raymond James does not lead with the highest transition check but leads with culture and capabilities, requiring competitive economics while offering a differentiated value proposition, and remaining disciplined on transition assistance and advisor economics.

On the fiscal 4Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), management said the firm is focused on the long term and providing a stable platform, attracting and retaining advisors with unique culture, leading service and robust platform rather than the largest check.

On the fiscal 4Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), management said Raymond James values independence to foster an environment where advisors can provide objective advice, unlike competitors that change comp plans each year to cross-sell bank products.

On the fiscal 3Q26 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2026), management said the firm has the largest addressable market in the industry because it offers all affiliation options and is agnostic about how advisors affiliate, wanting them drawn to its culture, values, platform and capabilities.

On the fiscal 2Q26 earnings call (period ended March 31, 2026), management said advisors do not have to choose between culture and capabilities, offering a unique combination of an advisor- and client-focused culture with leading technology, products and solutions.

On the fiscal 1Q26 earnings call (period ended December 31, 2025), management said the firm has the largest addressable market across its affiliation options (employee to independent contractor to RIA custody) with critical mass and decades of experience in all of them.

On the fiscal 1Q26 earnings call (period ended December 31, 2025), management described advisor recruiting as a long-term effort rather than a sprint, saying the firm must have a competitive check but wants advisors who want to stay long term and be satisfied over the rest of their careers.

On the fiscal 3Q26 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2026), management said consistency is a critical concept in recruiting and retaining advisors, focusing on finding advisors who are good cultural fits across affiliation options.

On the fiscal 1Q25 earnings call (period ended December 31, 2024), management described a value proposition combining the scope and breadth of products and capabilities to serve complex client needs with a strong culture anchored on putting people first.

On the fiscal 4Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), management said its strong balance sheet and commitment to independence are proving to be a differentiator for advisors evaluating alternatives.

Trade press (published September 29, 2026) reports that CEO Paul Shoukry and Elwyn said the advisor, not the home office, is the client, and that Shoukry has emphasized the firm's strategy of building its advisory ranks through individualized recruitment rather than large-scale acquisitions, evaluating each prospective advisor one-on-one.
